bib.title: Is Cosine-Similarity of Embeddings Really About Similarity?

question: Why does cosine similarity of learned embeddings sometimes work worse than the unnormalized dot product, and can it give arbitrary results?
hypothesis: Cosine similarity of embeddings from models trained on a dot-product objective depends on an arbitrary rescaling of latent dimensions that the regularization may leave free.
contributions: Analytical derivation for linear MF models that cosine similarity can be arbitrary or non-unique under one regularization (Eq. 1) and unique under another (Eq. 2)
Remedies and alternatives to cosine similarity

method.summary: Closed-form analysis of two L2-regularized linear matrix-factorization objectives (product-norm vs separate-norm), showing a free diagonal rescaling D changes embedding cosine similarities under the first. A simulated clustered user-item dataset illustrates item-item cosine similarity under different rescalings.
method.task: embedding similarity analysis (linear MF / linear autoencoder, simulated recommender data)

datasets.name: Simulated user-item interactions
datasets.size: n = 20,000 users, p = 1,000 items, C = 5 item clusters
datasets.preprocessing: Cluster probabilities p_c; per-cluster powerlaw exponent beta_c ~ Unif(0.25, 1.5); item baseline popularity PowerLaw(beta_c); user-cluster preferences sampled randomly; p_ui = p_uc(i) p_i / sum_i p_uc(i) p_i; per-user item count k_u ~ PowerLaw(beta_user = 0.5); k_u items sampled without replacement

models.name: Linear MF / linear autoencoder X ~ X A B^T
models.architecture: linear low-rank, A,B in R^{p x k}

training.objective: Eq.1: min ||X - XAB^T||_F^2 + lambda ||AB^T||_F^2; Eq.2: min ||X - XAB^T||_F^2 + lambda(||XA||_F^2 + ||B||_F^2); closed-form solutions via SVD
training.regularisation: lambda = 10,000 for Eq. 1; lambda = 100 for Eq. 2

inference.samples: one simulated dataset; number of runs not stated

parameters.rescalings_Eq1: three choices of diagonal D shown in Fig 1 (values only in figure labels, not in text)

metrics.name: item-item cosine similarity vs ground-truth cluster structure
metrics.definition: qualitative visual comparison of cosSim(B,B) heatmaps with ground-truth clusters (Fig 1)

eval.protocol: qualitative inspection only; no quantitative metric, no repeats stated

results.claim: For a full-rank model under Eq. 1 with one choice of D, all item-item cosine similarities between distinct items are zero.
results.setup: Analytical, full-rank k = p, objective Eq. 1, D = dMat(1/(1+lambda/sigma_i^2))^(1/2)

results.claim: Different D give different cosine similarities although the learned model AB^T is unchanged, so the results are arbitrary and not unique for Eq. 1.

results.claim: Eq. 2 (separate L2 on XA and B) gives a unique solution up to rotation, so its cosine similarities are unique.
results.quote: Hence, the cosine-similarity applied to the learned embeddings of this MF variant yields unique results.

results.claim: On simulated clustered data, item-item cosine similarities vary vastly across reasonable rescalings under Eq. 1 and differ again from the Eq. 2 solution.
results.setup: n=20,000 users, p=1,000 items, C=5 clusters, k=50, lambda=10,000 (Eq.1) and 100 (Eq.2); qualitative Fig 1
results.quote: here is to illustrate how vastly different the resulting cosine-similarities can be

limits: Only linear models are analysed; deep models are conjectured to be affected similarly or worse, not shown
Experiments are on simulated data only, qualitative, one figure, no quantitative metric or repeats
Authors say they know of no good metric for semantic similarity
Remedies (train on cosine, layer norm, project back to input space, normalize or debias before/during learning) are only suggested, not tested
Unique Eq. 2 solution is not shown to give the best semantic similarity
No retrieval/RAG or text-embedding experiments, so applicability to ANN search is inferred
